line_items.reasoning: FY'25 adjusted EPS guidance was cut again to $18.00–$18.60 from the prior $19.00–$20.00 range, falling well short of the midpoint FDX had guided to last quarter.

The revenue-net-of-costs headwind widened by $400M to $1.1B for FY'25, driven by yield pressure and demand mix shift, indicating revenue came in below even the low-end flat-to-slight-decline scenario guided last quarter.

Federal Express adjusted operating income grew 17% YoY (a beat on that segment), but FedEx Freight operating profit declined $80M YoY with continued headwinds, falling short of the guided margin contraction expectation in magnitude and trajectory.
FY'25 CapEx was reduced to $4.9B versus the guided $5.2B, coming in better (lower) than the reaffirmed target.
DRIVE savings reached $600M in Q3 (up from $540M in Q2 and $390M in Q1), confirming the sequential build and keeping the $2.2B incremental FY'25 target firmly on track as guided.
